facilities.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Transparent production sprite atlas of roadside BUILDINGS for an original 16-bit pixel-art road trip RPG on alien-occupied Earth.
Reference image is STYLE ONLY: match its sophisticated hand-crafted pixel art, crisp pixel clusters, material shading, teal/rust/amber color language, and swept black-violet alien technology. DO NOT copy its scenery or sky.
Create ONE image, extremely wide 3072x1024 if possible, with EXACTLY EIGHT fully separate building sprites arranged in an EXACT FOUR-COLUMN by TWO-ROW grid. Every cell identical size, row-major order below. No visible grid, no frames, no labels, no letters, NO background whatsoever. TRUE TRANSPARENT ALPHA background, including space between sprites and around doors. No white, grey, checkerboard, colored matte or painted ground plane. Each building complete and isolated. No sprite touches or crosses any cell edge. About 8% transparent padding around every building. Every building rests at the same baseline within its cell, and is composed as a wide horizontal building silhouette. Slight front elevation depth is allowed, but mostly SIDE-ON/front façade orthographic game view, NOT isometric aerial.
Art quality: much more refined than geometric placeholders. Distinct roofs, broken plaster, corrugated metal, dirty window glass, metal frames, small pipes, warm lit doorway, climbing vines, improvised survivor repairs. Strong readable masses and intentional pixel detailing. Opaque building surfaces only, no floating shadows outside silhouette. No people, vehicles, foreground roads, scenery or interface.
The world has been conquered by aliens. Each human facility has a SMALL black-violet crescent surveillance device mounted on its roof, with a few amber energy lights; otherwise it remains recognizably a survivor-maintained human facility. Avoid turning every building into the same science fiction tower. The checkpoint alone is overwhelmingly alien.
EIGHT sprites in EXACT row-major order:
TOP LEFT cell 1: survivor gasoline station, low teal-and-rust concrete shop with flat canopy and two weathered fuel pumps; hoses, broken canopy lights, no sign lettering.
TOP row cell 2: garage repair workshop, broad corrugated iron gable roof, large dark open service bay, tool rack visible inside, rusted exhaust pipes, no parked cars.
TOP row cell 3: small roadside motel, two-level weathered cream-and-rust building, several warm-lit windows, exterior staircase, water tank, a battered blank sign silhouette.
TOP RIGHT cell 4: medical clinic, modest pale concrete building with a green cross SYMBOL, patched awning, glass entrance, oxygen tanks and emergency lamp.
BOTTOM LEFT cell 5: pharmacy, narrow inviting green storefront with medicine bottle shapes behind glass, green cross SYMBOL, rolling shutters partly open, rooftop alien monitor.
BOTTOM row cell 6: warehouse, broad rusted hangar with sliding metal doors, a few crates at the doorway, loading ramp, cables, corrugated roof.
BOTTOM row cell 7: survivor general store, warmly lit red-brown storefront, canvas awning, baskets and supplies beneath windows, patched roof, no text.
BOTTOM RIGHT cell 8: ALIEN OCCUPATION CHECKPOINT, tall swept black-violet crescent arch above passage, asymmetric layered biomechanical armor, amber-lit segmented barrier and small hovering sensor integrated into silhouette, dangerous and unmistakably nonhuman.
Eight different complete isolated sprites, consistent scale and art quality. No writing, numerals, captions, logos, watermarks, people, cars, roads, background or grid lines. True transparency is mandatory.

interiors.initialPrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: eight-room background atlas for a finished original pixel-art JRPG on alien-occupied Earth.
Reference image is visual STYLE ONLY: match sophisticated 16-bit pixel clusters, crisp readable silhouettes, textured materials, restrained teal/navy/coral/rust and warm amber glow, cinematic atmosphere. This is not an illustration page or UI mockup. Create game backgrounds.
Create EXACTLY EIGHT rectangular interior scene panels in an exact TWO-COLUMN by FOUR-ROW equal grid. Overall image approximately 1536x1408, almost square but slightly wider; each individual panel is a WIDE panoramic room around 768x352, ratio 2.18:1. Full bleed, no gutters, no framing, no border lines, absolutely no writing, signage lettering, numbers, titles or UI. Scenes must not cross their rectangular grid boundaries.
All scenes side-on / front-facing JRPG room background, like standing inside a room looking toward rear wall. No overhead or isometric view. Bottom 30% of EACH PANEL must be open unobstructed floor for separately animated characters and event props. Furniture belongs mostly against back wall or along sides; leave the central floor clear. No characters, no creatures, no vehicles, no foreground event objects in the walking area.
The world was conquered by aliens years ago; spaces remain recognizably human but each contains some curved black-violet alien monitoring device, amber-lit parasite cable, or adapted alien tech. Designs detailed, beautiful, legible at a small mobile game size. Avoid excessive clutter. Consistent strong ambient occlusion, carefully placed highlights, original hand-crafted pixel-art feeling, not crude blocks, not a 3D render, not a photograph, not blurry.
Eight rooms in exact reading order:
ROW 1 LEFT: WAREHOUSE — worn concrete brick back wall, tall steel shelving with crates and tarps around side walls, high clerestory window, suspended amber lamp, alien cable entering a wall vent; large clear central concrete floor.
ROW 1 RIGHT: CLINIC — pale mint tile, a survivor clinic with one empty bed along far left back wall, cabinet of bandages, sinks, patched medicine curtains and tiny alien surveillance pod, tranquil warm lamplight; clear floor across bottom.
ROW 2 LEFT: GARAGE — corrugated metal workshop, tools arranged on wall, industrial lift posts along sides, hanging hoses, oil-dark concrete, amber lamp, alien power source on rear workbench; no car and central floor empty.
ROW 2 RIGHT: SHOP — warm survivor general store, packed wooden shelves against rear wall, canvas and repaired counter at one edge, hanging lanterns, canned supplies and small monitor on back wall; clear foreground.
ROW 3 LEFT: HOTEL — abandoned but usable motel lobby, worn wallpaper, threadbare armchair at far side, reception desk against back wall, closed doors, warm sconce lighting, subtle alien wire vines; open floor.
ROW 3 RIGHT: LABORATORY — occupied human lab with violet biomechanical equipment attached to pale clinical cabinets, glowing translucent amber sample vessels along back wall, black crescent observation lens suspended high, cool teal light; no monsters and clear floor.
ROW 4 LEFT: RUIN — cracked plaster and exposed masonry interior, broken roof exposing a shaft of daylight, rubble only at room edges, old damaged window with alien skyline faintly beyond, dusty yet gorgeous atmosphere; broad clear dusty stone floor.
ROW 4 RIGHT: NEST — recognizable ruined room gradually engulfed by alien ecology: huge teal glowing fungi against back wall, pulsing amber sacs attached to wall, violet sinewy roots around ceiling and sides, otherworldly soft glow; dark empty central floor, NO creatures or characters.
No text, labels, frames, people, enemies, UI or foreground obstructions. Every grid cell has an open usable lower floor band.

Keep EXACTLY TWO COLUMNS and FOUR ROWS of equally sized panels. Thus EACH PANEL is a 2:1 wide rectangular room, not the overly wide 3:1 panels in the reference.
Preserve the same eight rooms in the same reading order and the same polished pixel-art aesthetic: warehouse, clinic; garage, shop; hotel, laboratory; ruin, alien nest. Preserve recognizable material shading, amber/cyan lighting, dark curved alien apparatus, warm survivor interior details. Redraw their composition for the new less-wide individual panel framing rather than squeezing or stretching the old art. Room main subjects centered; furniture mostly along rear wall and sides. Bottom 30% of each panel empty floor for game characters. No characters, no monsters, no cars, no UI, no words, no labels, no grid lines or panel borders. True original 16-bit pixel art. Clean distinct panel boundaries, no gutters. Output one square 2-by-4 atlas.

inspection: All eight facility and room subjects visible in correct order, shared pixel-art style, no text or UI, transparent alpha verified for facilities. Raw final PNG files copied unchanged.
